presentingComplaint: Two days of worsening confusion, nausea and unsteadiness, with a witnessed brief seizure at home.
history: Retired factory supervisor and ex-smoker (45 pack-years) brought in by family with 48 hours of increasing drowsiness, poor concentration, nausea without vomiting blood, headache and an unsteady, staggering gait. A brief generalised seizure occurred this morning. Over the preceding two months he has had a dry cough and 6 kg of unintentional weight loss. Background of type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin and gliclazide, last HbA1c 7.4%) and CKD stage 3b (baseline creatinine ~1.8 mg/dL). No diuretics; family GP recently started him on a proton-pump inhibitor. Fluid intake normal, no vomiting or diarrhoea, no polyuria or excessive thirst, no chest pain or breathlessness at rest. No alcohol excess.
examination: Drowsy but rousable, GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6), disoriented to time. Clinically euvolaemic: moist mucous membranes, JVP not raised, no peripheral oedema, no ascites, normal skin turgor, capillary refill <2s. No postural hypotension. Chest: reduced air entry right upper zone, no crackles or wheeze. Cardiovascular and abdominal exam unremarkable. Mild gait ataxia; no focal limb weakness, no neck stiffness, plantars flexor, no asterixis.
imaging: Chest radiograph: right hilar/perihilar mass with right upper zone volume loss. CT head (non-contrast): no haemorrhage, mass or acute infarct; consistent with metabolic encephalopathy. Staging CT chest recommended for suspected bronchogenic malignancy.
microbiology: Not applicable — no infective focus; septic screen not indicated on clinical grounds.
differentialDiagnoses: SIADH (euvolaemic hypotonic hyponatraemia), likely paraneoplastic from a bronchogenic (small-cell) tumour
Hyperglycaemia-related (translocational) hyponatraemia / HHS — excluded: glucose only mildly raised, corrected Na still 112, osmolality low
Hypervolaemic hyponatraemia from heart failure — no oedema, no raised JVP, no orthopnoea
CKD-related dilutional hyponatraemia — degree far exceeds CKD stage 3b expectation
finalDiagnosis: Severe symptomatic hyponatraemia (Na 111 mmol/L) due to SIADH, most likely paraneoplastic from an underlying lung malignancy; diabetes and CKD are confounders that must be excluded before anchoring on SIADH.
citations: European Society of Endocrinology — Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyponatraemia — 2014
American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care in Diabetes (hyperglycaemic crises) — 2024
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Disorders of Sodium and Water Balance / Paraneoplastic Syndromes
stewardship: Not applicable — non-infective metabolic emergency; no antibiotics indicated. 'Stewardship' here is diagnostic and therapeutic restraint: establish true volume status and hypotonic state before treatment, avoid unnecessary saline boluses, and above all avoid overly rapid sodium correction.
contraindications: Do NOT correct sodium faster than 8 mmol/L in 24h (or 4-6 mmol/L if very high osmotic demyelination risk) — malnourished ex-smoker is high-risk
Avoid 0.9% saline as sole therapy in SIADH — may worsen hyponatraemia when urine osmolality exceeds infusate osmolality
Avoid gliclazide-driven hypoglycaemia masking the picture; recheck glucose
Fluid restriction alone is inadequate for acute symptomatic (seizure) presentation — needs hypertonic saline
edgeCases: Symptomatic (seizure) hyponatraemia warrants 100-150 mL boluses of 3% hypertonic saline regardless of chronicity to raise Na 4-6 mmol/L acutely
Corrected sodium for glucose reclassifies apparent hyperglycaemic hyponatraemia; here correction is negligible, confirming true hypotonicity
Low serum uric acid (<4 mg/dL) and high fractional excretion of urate support SIADH over other causes
CKD blunts urinary dilution/concentration — interpret urine osmolality with caution, but 512 mOsm/kg with low serum osmolality is still inappropriate
expectedMaiK: Euvolaemic, hypotonic hyponatraemia (low serum osmolality) with inappropriately concentrated urine (osm >100), urine Na >30, low uric acid, and normal thyroid/adrenal/renal-adjusted status = SIADH; exclude the diabetes (glucose correction) and CKD confounders, then treat symptomatic Na 111 with cautious hypertonic saline while investigating an underlying lung malignancy.
expectedNextQuestions: What is the true volume status (JVP, oedema, postural BP, mucous membranes)?
Any diuretics, PPI, SSRI, carbamazepine or other drugs precipitating SIADH?
Is there weight loss, cough, haemoptysis or smoking history suggesting malignancy?
How acute is the drop — any prior sodium results to gauge chronicity and demyelination risk?
expectedInvestigations: Paired serum and urine osmolality with urine sodium
9am cortisol and TSH to exclude adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism
Serum uric acid and renal function (contextualise for CKD)
Chest imaging (CXR then staging CT) to seek occult malignancy
regressionAssertions: Engine must rank hyponatremia first given euvolaemic hypotonic hyponatraemia with concentrated urine and high urine sodium
Must not anchor on hhs — glucose-corrected sodium remains ~112 with low serum osmolality
Must flag risk of osmotic demyelination and cap correction at 8 mmol/L/24h
Must recommend no antibiotics (non-infective) and set stewardship tier null
Must trigger malignancy work-up given weight loss, smoking history and hilar mass
